subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
A PERMUTATION WHOSE ATOMS ARE ALL PURE REGISTER-FIELD DIFFERENCES IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY CENSUS THIS PROJECT HAS BUILT, AND IT IS WHAT TURNS A NON-BIJECTIVE RECOLOR INTO A BIJECTIVE ONE. cn_census, ch_census26, hb_census and my own run-27 filter all derive their permutation windows from the UNABSORBED words -- those that are neither identical nor a pure register-field difference. That is correct for the schedule class and STRUCTURALLY BLIND to this one: such a window contributes ZERO unabsorbed words, forms no cluster, and is never proposed. The population is not hypothetical. HB measured 93 Tier-A functions image-wide, found 70 that pass verify_consistent_recolor and observed that all 70 were already shipped, correctly concluding the zero-permutation payoff was harvested. The other 23 -- the Tier-A functions that REFUSE the recolor -- were never worked, because a Tier-A refusal reads as 'the recolor is not a renaming' when what it actually means is 'the recolor is not a renaming AT THIS SCHEDULE'.

THE MECHANISM, in one sentence. When our build and the target both materialise two interchangeable values (two `li rD,0`, two `mr rD,r3`) and assign them to each other's registers, the positional renaming is TWO-VALUED at the first CFG merge that joins them, verify_consistent_recolor intersects the disagreeing bindings away, and the refusal surfaces at some later USE -- often hundreds of words downstream of the actual cause. Transposing the two definitions makes the SAME recolor a clean bijection, with no other change to the rule.

THE REFUSAL OFFSET IS A POINTER, NOT A VERDICT. This is the operative reading rule and it is the opposite of what the message invites. `+0xNN: use of gX does not correspond to gY under the running renaming` names the merge where the two-valued binding was OBSERVED; the repair lives at the pair of definitions UPSTREAM of it. Search upstream contiguous windows, require the order to be shape- and relocation-consistent and legal in OUR colouring standing alone (claim.law.C1_...v1 step 0, since apply_patch runs the permutation first), and select by proof through apply_patch. A candidate that merely MOVES the refusal further down the function is progress and should be kept and iterated, not discarded.

WORKED MEMBER, SHIPPED: game/world/tower::TowerCheckMessages, 697 instructions, real 122 -> 0. All 122 differing words are pure register-field differences, so copy_register_fields alone reproduces the target bytes, and it refused anyway. ONE two-atom window, [0x430,0x438) order [1,0], accepted by check_permutation_dependences in its strictest form with exit_dead=None and carrying no relocation in either object, makes the whole function verify. A 697-instruction exact from a two-word transposition that no census could nominate.

WORKED NON-MEMBER, AND ITS BAR IS THE GENERAL ONE: game/sys/memcard::drawMemCardMessage, 204 instructions, real 126. Its first refusal at +0x84 IS this class and IS repaired -- window [0x24,0x2c) order [1,0] transposes our two zero-inits (`li r26,0` / `li r29,0` against the target's `li r26,0` / `li r22,0`) and the refusal moves to +0x1ec. That second refusal is NOT this class and no repair reaches it: at +0x1ec we read r28 where the target reads r25, and a control path exists (measured, +0xf4 branches to +0x108, skipping the defining +0xcc) on which NEITHER register is defined inside the function. Both sides read an incoming callee-saved value, so recolouring would change WHICH caller register the value comes from, and the guard is right to refuse. THE DISCRIMINATOR, applicable before any search: take the refusing use, take the definition that should bind it, and ask whether a path from entry reaches the use while AVOIDING that definition. If no, the binding was lost to a schedule difference and this class applies. If yes, the correspondence rests on an uninitialised register and no permutation reaches it.

COST AND YIELD. The search is a handful of apply_patch calls per round over contiguous 2-to-4-atom upstream windows; it found the TowerCheckMessages repair in one round. Ten unshipped Tier-A candidates were available in this lane's half; two closed. Any lane holding a Tier-A refusal should run this before recording a cap, and any census that reports a Tier-A refusal count should stop treating that count as a residue.
